clue.text: Leaves them covered in ink from it

definitions.text: Leaves them covered in ink from it

parts.words: Leaves them covered in ink from it
parts.note: leaves are sheets of paper, which come out of a machine inked with type

explanation.surface: Something drops foliage that is smothered in ink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' suggests trees or departing, but here it means the pages of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine for printing transfers ink onto sheets of paper, the leaves of a book.

clue.text: It's good not to be round shouldered, etc

definitions.text: It's good not to be round shouldered, etc

parts.words: It's good not to be round shouldered, etc
parts.note: describes the way the body is held, which is good when one stands straight

explanation.surface: Advice against slouching.
explanation.definitionFit: Good bearing of the body means not hunching the shoulders; that bearing is the word for how one carries oneself.

clue.text: Mind how you put it up!

definitions.text: Mind how you put it up!

parts.words: Mind how you put it up!
parts.note: read as putting something up into a church steeple, and also as raising the mind or spirits

explanation.surface: A warning to take care when erecting something.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as IN SPIRE, something put up into a church steeple; whole, it means to stir the mind.
explanation.definitionFit: To stimulate the mind or lift the spirits is the sense of the verb, with a steeple joke on the side.

clue.text: They won't wear sitting for an artist

definitions.text: They won't wear sitting for an artist

parts.words: They won't wear sitting for an artist
parts.note: models who pose for a painter wearing no clothes

explanation.surface: Life models who keep their clothes off while posing.
explanation.definitionFit: Unclothed figures posing for painters are the subject of many artworks known by this plural term.

clue.text: Said flattering things to people about despair

definitions.text: Said flattering things to people

indicators.note: about means moved around, so the letters of despair are shuffled

explanation.surface: Someone flattered people who were in despair.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking approvingly of someone is the past tense verb for complimenting them.

clue.text: Turned out? .Well, that's what it means

definitions.text: Turned out? .Well, that's what it means

parts.words: Turned out? .Well, that's what it means
parts.note: joining the words across the question mark gives the phrase well turned out, meaning smartly dressed

explanation.surface: A rhetorical exchange about what something proved to be.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the two halves together: 'well turned out' is a stylish person.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone well turned out is smartly dressed and graceful, which is the adjective's sense.

clue.text: Don't want to be committed, so put bottom on railings!

definitions.text: Don't want to be committed
definitions.meaning: to stay neutral, refusing to take a side

definitions.text: put bottom on railings!
definitions.meaning: literally to perch on a barrier

explanation.surface: An uncommitted person literally perched on a fence.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for avoiding taking sides pictures a person perched on a boundary between two fields.

clue.text: Starts an argument with a logician! Is the second character first, as it goes between

definitions.text: Starts an argument with a logician!

indicators.note: the word as is placed between the two other pieces

parts.note: B is the second letter of the alphabet
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A logician begins a debate by playing with the alphabet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second character' means the second letter of the alphabet, not a person in a story; 'first' puts that letter at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: The foundation from which a logician starts reasoning is the premise underlying the argument.

clue.text: The first to try to get fortune like this

definitions.text: The first to try to get fortune like this

parts.words: The first to try to get fortune like this
parts.note: a novice who succeeds at a first attempt

explanation.surface: Fortune that comes to those trying something new.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the surprising success often enjoyed by novices at a first attempt.

clue.text: Gives promise to Lord Protector having responsibility for child's spiritual welfare

definitions.text: having responsibility for child's spiritual welfare

parts.note: the Lord is God
a parent protects a child

explanation.surface: Cromwell, the Lord Protector, makes a promise at a christening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lord Protector' looks like Cromwell's title but splits into two pieces. 'Gives promise to' recalls the vows made at baptism.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponsor at a christening vows to oversee the child's religious upbringing.

clue.text: Motor cyclist's pupils covered by such insurance against harm

definitions.text: Motor cyclist's pupils covered by such insurance against harm

parts.words: Motor cyclist's pupils covered by such insurance against harm
parts.note: pupils are the eyes' centres, shielded by protective eyewear

explanation.surface: A motorcyclist's students have an insurance policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pupils' suggests learners but means the eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: Protective eyewear worn by riders shields the eyes from wind and debris.

clue.text: Vicious fighter taking his eyes off an opponent like this

definitions.text: Vicious fighter taking his eyes off an opponent like this

parts.words: Vicious fighter taking his eyes off an opponent like this
parts.note: taking the eyes off literally, by digging them out, rather than looking away

explanation.surface: A fighter loses focus on an opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking his eyes off' sounds like distraction; here it means literally removing the opponent's eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: Digging out an opponent's eyes with the thumbs is a brutal fighting act.

clue.text: Keep up support for the Mark in America

definitions.text: Keep up support

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for America within the word for a mark

parts.note: a stain is a mark
US is the United States

explanation.surface: Ongoing backing for a man named Mark living in the States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a name but is a blemish, STAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain backing over time is to keep something going, a synonym.

clue.text: Sounds like biscuit for a relative

definitions.text: relative

indicators.note: says the word for a biscuit is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a Nice is a coconut biscuit popular in Britain, its name said like the French city

explanation.surface: A biscuit standing in for a family member.
explanation.walkthrough: A Nice biscuit is a sugared coconut biscuit sold in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's daughter is a family member.

clue.text: Finally fight here

definitions.text: Finally fight here

parts.note: the place of a final stand, from fighting to the very end

explanation.surface: Instruction to fight at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperate final effort is named after the trench where defenders made their final stand.

clue.text: For the jockey's sake, they back the horses, as it were!

definitions.text: For the jockey's sake, they back the horses, as it were!

parts.words: For the jockey's sake, they back the horses, as it were!
parts.note: they sit on the backs of horses for riders, not bets placed on them

explanation.surface: Punters backing horses to help the jockey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back the horses' suggests betting, but these sit on horses' backs.
explanation.definitionFit: Riders' seats strapped onto horses' backs make the ride possible.

clue.text: Put into words the meaning of: "sent fast"

definitions.text: Put into words
sent fast

explanation.surface: A definition being looked up.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: something stated in speech, and post sent by special fast delivery.

clue.text: Hasn't much space to grow pulse food, this worker

definitions.text: Hasn't much space to grow

parts.note: peas are pulses
a worker is an ant, in crossword convention

explanation.surface: A labourer with little room to raise vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this worker' looks like the definition, but ANT is the worker; the smallholder is defined by the land.
explanation.definitionFit: A small farmer typically works a tiny plot of land.

clue.text: Language second to none? On the contrary, to most

definitions.text: Language second to none? On the contrary, to most

parts.words: Language second to none? On the contrary, to most
parts.note: a tongue that is a second language for most speakers worldwide

explanation.surface: A boast that a language is the best.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second to none' sounds like praise; it is literally a second language for most of its users.
explanation.definitionFit: The world's most used second language is spoken by more non-native than native speakers.

clue.text: Outspoken poker player may try it on

definitions.text: Outspoken
poker player may try it on
definitions.meaning: a deceptive bet made to pretend a strong hand

explanation.surface: A forthright card player attempts a deception.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: blunt and hearty in manner, and the deception used at the card table.

clue.text: Got wrong job

definitions.text: Got wrong job

parts.note: a job made a mess of, or the wrong job taken

explanation.surface: Someone was given the wrong post.
explanation.definitionFit: A botched task is one carried out clumsily, a near synonym of messed up.

clue.text: Presumably such food set on the left side of the table?

definitions.text: Presumably such food set on the left side of the table?

parts.words: Presumably such food set on the left side of the table?
parts.note: food left on the plate, playing on left meaning the side

explanation.surface: A question about where food is placed at a table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' is a side, but food 'left' is not consumed.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that remains on the plate has not been consumed.

clue.text: Given torrent of abuse about Dan's leg

definitions.text: Given torrent of abuse

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone was abused over Dan's leg.
explanation.definitionFit: Verbally attacked with insults, the British informal past tense for abusing someone.

clue.text: A way to die from deep breathing, one might say

definitions.text: A way to die from deep breathing, one might say

parts.words: A way to die from deep breathing, one might say
parts.note: breathing in the deep, meaning the sea, underwater

explanation.surface: A warning that deep breaths can kill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deep' is the sea, not a full breath.
explanation.definitionFit: Dying by inhaling water is the meaning of the verb.

clue.text: Slides into this magic place after the pictures!

definitions.text: Slides into this magic place after the pictures!

parts.words: Slides into this magic place after the pictures!
parts.note: the magic one was an old slide projector

explanation.surface: Someone slips into a magical spot after the cinema.
explanation.walkthrough: 'magic' plus the answer names the early slide projector; 'Slides' is not a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: A magic version of this light source projected glass slides as early shows.

clue.text: For all in the committee or against!

definitions.text: For all in the committee or against!

parts.words: For all in the committee or against!
parts.note: every member votes the same way, whether for or against

explanation.surface: A committee vote.
explanation.definitionFit: When every member agrees, a vote is described by this adjective.

clue.text: By which we can buy French wine without a retail problem

definitions.text: By which we can buy French wine

indicators.note: a problem leaves the letters jumbled, rearranged after the a is removed

explanation.surface: Buying French wine without trouble at the shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' takes A from RETAIL, and 'problem' rearranges what is left, RETIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A metric unit of volume is how wine is sold in France.

clue.text: Need king chart new place for vegetables?

definitions.text: place for vegetables

indicators.note: new means remade, so the letters of the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Does a king need a new chart for his vegetables?
explanation.definitionFit: A plot for growing vegetables for the household is named for the room where food is cooked.
